thread.title: Sand In My Shoes - My Very Late May Update

author: Brian Soule
title: Sand In My Shoes - My Very Late May Update
text:
I want to apologize right up front to all my faithful readers that this is so late. Early June has been a whirlwind for the Soule family. The eldest Soule child has graduated from high school (and there was much rejoicing). In fact, that’s what it was. There was much rejoicing. Family was in town, there was the preparation for the party and the visitors, a week-long vacation with the new graduate took place immediately after the graduation festivities, and to top it off the following week yours truly went to be a leader at a Boy Scout summer camp and just arrived back home this past weekend. So, the time to write has been very, very limited and I have missed it.
Truly the last three to four weeks I have paid almost no attention to my portfolio. I do know that dividends have continued to roll in even though I have been tuned out. This is comforting and one of the great charms of this thing we call “Dividend Growth Investing”. The income received from these companies we purchase a small ( very small) piece of is truly passive income in every sense of the word. I have done nothing, or almost nothing, as far as this portfolio is concerned, yet I have received literally hundreds of dollars in passive income in the past 3-4 weeks.
One of the other charms of this form of investing is that I will continue to get a raise from these companies assuming I have done my research and made intelligent and informed decisions.
So without further ado, I will jump right in to the May reporting.
May Dividends
All graphs and charts created by author unless otherwise specified
In May, my dividends collected reached $259.02, an all-time high. This was due mainly to two reasons. First, my purchase in March of 16 more units of Magellan Midstream Partners LP ( MMP ) and the doubling of my Realty Income Corp. (NYSE: O ) position. These moves added about twenty-five bucks to my May income (over February). Secondly, I received a dividend from a new position of mine, Air Products and Chemicals Inc. ( APD ), and a dividend increase from Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), which combined for about another twenty bucks over my February number. All in all, a very good month for dividends for the Sand in Shoes portfolio compared to February.
Even more fun, this May was up over $170 compared to the same month last year. See below.
May Performance
Finally, we had an up month, and I am almost back to even on a YTD basis. Happy and excited to have a month of 1% plus growth in the value of the portfolio. More exciting to me as a dividend growth investor, however, is that the stream of dividends pouring into my account continues to grow.
Individual Stocks The table below shows my positions as of close of business on May 31, 2018:
There are three stocks with yields below 2.0%, which is less than optimum. As for AAPL, that's just what it's going to be for a little while. However, AAPL is a fairly new dividend growth stock and the raises have been pretty substantial the past five years. Given their hoard of cash and the geyser of free cash flow they produce, I expect the hefty dividend raises to continue for the foreseeable future, which is one of the main reasons I own the stock.
I am expecting some time in the next month for both Bank of America Corp. ( BAC ) and Citigroup Inc. ( C ) to substantially raise their dividends similar to what they did last year. For a discussion on that (and a horribly embarrassing discussion of my AIG purchase), please see this article from last June.
Projected Dividends I added a new position in May as I indicated, but have not had the time to finish the article yet (stay tuned). The stock is International Flavors & Fragrances Inc. ( IFF ) and is the second stock from the materials sector in the portfolio. The first dividend I will receive for that position is in July, so you won't see that reflected in the table below.
The total projected dividends for the year are now solidly over $2,000. I'll try to remember to post the yearly projection next month so you can see that.
The second quarter will be the highest total yet, and is a little strange because both Bank of America Corp. and PepsiCo ( PEP ) will pay me twice in Q2. The hope is that with added positions and dividend hikes, the third quarter will beat the second one out anyway. Time will tell.
Sector Diversification The addition of IFF brought the materials sector, which was the lowest percentage at just around 4%, up to 7.3%. The next most under-represented sectors are Telecom (5.2%) and Utilities (5.8%). Don't be surprised if some time during the month of June I add some more shares of AT&T ( T ) or Southern Company ( SO ) or some other stock in either of those two sectors.
Consumer Discretionary 9.4% Consumer Staples 10.1% Energy 7.4% Financials 17.3% Health Care 10.2% Industrials 6.4% Materials 7.3% REIT 12.8% Technology 8.2% Telecom 5.2% Utilities 5.8% 100% Asset Allocation of the Portfolio
My domestic fixed income percentage has slipped below the level where I would like to address it. It is down to 27.3% as of May 31 compared to last month where it sat at 27.7% (spoiler alert - it dropped further before I finally added funds to that asset class last week, stay tuned for the June update to see the specifics).
Also, small cap stocks have been on fire lately, and while I did not intend to trim around the edges of a piece of my portfolio that only makes up 5% of the total, I could pull about $1,000 out of small caps and $500 out of mid caps and still maintain the 5% target. That might be something I look at doing if the trend continues. I do not pay a commission on certain ETFs so the transactions would be completely painless.
But for May, I did not make any changes to the asset allocation of the portfolio.
Sales and Purchases in May As mentioned above, there was one new position added (IFF). On May 24th, I purchased 16 shares at $124.90 per share. As I write this, the stock is trading below $124, so I did not catch the bottom, but that means you have the opportunity to get in at a lower price than I did. I hope to have my article detailing the reasons I purchased the stock out by the end of this week, but you should be doing your own research anyway.
IFF data by YCharts
Final Thoughts I am very pleased with the progress. May was a good month from a total return perspective, but even more exciting is the over $250 in dividends in a single month. As you will see soon, and as I projected, the month of June will be pretty close to $250 as well. The new dividend rates will be in force in June from both Home Depot Inc. ( HD ) and PEP.
I now have more than one stock in seven of the eleven sectors, which is great. I will add new stocks as they become attractive, but there is nothing wrong with adding to existing positions when those become attractive as well. I now have 21 stocks with my ultimate goal being in the 25-30 range. I don't think that is too many to keep up with, along with the 6-10 that I am always watching and simply waiting for the time to be right to make a purchase.
I hope you enjoyed the article and following me on this journey. Please join me next month (or in a few days) as we close out the second quarter and look forward to the second half of the year. Thank you for reading and good luck!
Disclosure: I am/we are long AAPL, AIG, AMGN, APD, BAC, BLK, C, CSCO, CVS, GPC, HD, HRL, IFF, MMM, MMP, O, OHI, PEP, SO, T, WMT.
I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.
